title: More than 100,000 people in Japan are now aged 100 or older
byline: The number of people aged 100 or more in Japan has exceeded 100,000 for the first time, according to the health ministry.

title: Barnes Place property fraud: Suspect arrested
byline: The Financial Investigation Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested a suspect in connection with a large-scale land fraud involving a forged property deed in Barnes Place, Colombo 07.

title: Security tightened at Fort Magistrate’s Court ahead of Namal’s appearance
byline: Police have heightened security around the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court premises ahead of the scheduled appearance of Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa today (16).

title: Shiranthi Rajapaksa leaves for Singapore
byline: Former First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa departed for Singapore from the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in the early hours of today (16), airport sources said.

title: Misinformation on Aesthetic studies misleads society: experts
byline: “There is no use of the Arts, one can prosper by becoming a doctor or an engineer. Don’t think of studying the Arts but try to become a doctor or an engineer. This has been the mindset of most parents in Sri Lanka over the years and they have not encouraged their children to study the Arts. However, one must remember that the Arts could do much more than anyone could imagine.

title: Nalinda responds to President’s coriander remark
byline: Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa today clarified remarks by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake that drew criticism from the Opposition, saying the President was referring to reducing unnecessary visits to tertiary hospitals for primary healthcare needs.

title: High Court bail for drug cases involving less than 100g
byline: The Government is taking steps to amend the law to once again allow suspects arrested with less than 100 grams of drugs (gross) to seek bail from the High Court, Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara said yesterday.

title: Turkish Airlines to probe damage to Rumesh Tharanga’s equipment
byline: Sri Lankan civil aviation authorities have sought an explanation from Turkish Airlines over damage reportedly caused to the sports equipment of world champion javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga during his return journey to Sri Lanka. the Ministry of  Ports and Civil Aviation said.

title: Govt. has made no decision to reintroduce the death penalty
byline: Amid renewed calls to reintroduce the death penalty for organised crime in the wake of continuing shooting incidents, Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday that the Government had not taken any decision on the matter.

title: All Opposition parties to meet tomorrow for discussion on launching a common struggle to save democracy
byline: All opposition political parties are to meet tomorrow in Colombo for a discussion on launching a common struggle to safeguard democracy, Convenor Joint Opposition Professor G.L. Peiris said.

title: ’Positive sign for Indian investments in Colombo Port City’
byline: Positive talks between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the BRICS summit could make a positive symbolic gesture to ease concerns surrounding the Colombo Port City and create a more favourable environment to attract Indian investment, according to CHEC Port City Colombo Deputy Managing Director, Thulci Aluwihare.

title: Polgolla Reservoir to be emptied for repairs from Sept. 25
byline: The Polgolla Reservoir will be emptied for about two and a half days from midnight on September 25 to facilitate urgent repairs to its gates, the Water Management Secretariat said today.

title: RDA urges headlights on expressways
byline: The Road Development Authority (RDA) has urged motorists to switch on their headlights while travelling on expressways due to adverse weather conditions and reduced visibility.

title: Widespread rain expected across Sri Lanka over next 10 days
byline: Widespread rainfall is expected across the island over the next 10 days, while preparations should be made to face possible heavy rain, landslides and floods, the Meteorology Department said.

title: US House votes to end Iran war, 7 Republicans join in favour
byline: For a third time, the US House has voted to end the war in Iran, approving a war powers resolution that would halt President Donald Trump’s ability to continue military action without congressional approval.

title: ‘We are not afraid and will not flee’: Gnanasara Thera
byline: Bodu Bala Sena (BBS) General Secretary Ven. Galagodaaththe Gnanasara Thera, who appeared before the Colombo High Court today, said he would surrender to the court and abide by the law, insisting that he would not flee following the Supreme Court decision to annul the presidential pardon granted to him in 2019.

title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi drone headed for Mecca
byline: Saudi Arabia has said that a drone launched by the Houthis towards Mecca has been intercepted and destroyed, in an escalation that could threaten the holy city.

title: Did Shiranthi Rajapaksa leave country after FCID summons?
byline: Shiranthi Rajapaksa, wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa left the country earlier today despite being summoned to appear before the Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID).

title: Court issues warrants for Aravinda de Silva and wife
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today issued warrants for the arrest of former cricketer Aravinda de Silva and his wife, Priyanga Anushka Wijenayake.

title: Gnanasara Thera appears before Colombo High Court
byline: Bodu Bala Sena Secretary Ven. Galagodaaththe Gnanasara Thera appeared before the Colombo High Court today as the case filed against him by the Attorney General over alleged remarks insulting Islam was taken up.

title: Sri Lanka, Thailand move to expedite visa-free travel for ordinary passport holders
byline: Sri Lanka and Thailand have agreed to further strengthen bilateral relations, with discussions focusing on expediting arrangements for a visa exemption for ordinary passport holders.

title: US House advances 100% tariff bill targeting India, other Russian oil buyers
byline: The US House of Representatives has voted to advance a bill that would empower President Donald Trump to impose 100 per cent tariffs on India and other countries importing Russian oil and gas.

title: LAWASIA raises serious concerns over procedure in Supreme Court hearings on 22nd Amendment
byline: The Law Association for Asia and the Pacific (LAWASIA) has expressed serious concern over the procedure followed by the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka in the constitutional challenges to the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, which seeks to extend the retirement ages of Judges of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal.

title: More than 100,000 people in Japan are now aged 100 or older
byline: The number of people aged 100 or more in Japan has exceeded 100,000 for the first time, according to the health ministry.

title: 30,000 families at risk of landslides after cyclone Ditwah
byline: More than 30,000 families have been identified as being at risk of landslides following Cyclone Ditwah with the National Building Research Institute (NBRO) warning that even areas previously considered safe could now be vulnerable.

title: Kotmale power generation to stop from Sept. 26 night
byline: Power generation at the Kotmale Hydropower Plant will be suspended from 10 p.m. on September 26 until 2 p.m. on September 27 for maintenance work, Director of the Water Management Secretariat Engineer Nilantha Dhanapala said.

title: Seven railway services cancelled tonight
byline: The Railways Department has cancelled seven scheduled train services, including six night mail trains and one additional service.

title: EU opens door for Canada to become its first associate member, von der Leyen says
byline: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the European Union ​is opening the door for Canada to become its first ’’associate member’’, a ‌status that is not set out in the bloc’s treaties.

title: Namal Rajapaksa remanded
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who was named as a suspect and produced before court by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in connection with alleged financial irregularities and money laundering linked to the purchase of Airbus aircraft for SriLankan Airlines, was ordered to be remanded until September 23 by Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today.

title: Mannar hospital to get new Rs. 600 Mn Accident and Emergency Unit
byline: A new Rs. 600 million Accident and Emergency Treatment Unit is being constructed at the Mannar District General Hospital, with construction commencing today (16) under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: Sri Lanka Women’s squad named for 2026 Asian Games
byline: The Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) Selection Committee has officially announced a 15-member national squad to represent the island nation at the upcoming 2026 Asian Games.  The national women’s team will be led by veteran captain Chamari Athapaththu. Sri Lanka is set to begin their campaign on September 18, 2026, when they face the Malaysian Women’s team in the third quarter-final of the tournament.

title: Customs revenue surpasses Rs. 2 trillion
byline: Sri Lanka Customs has surpassed the Rs. 2 trillion mark in revenue collection, recording a significant milestone in its annual revenue performance.

title: Dudley Sirisena pledges annual javelins to support Rumesh Tharanga
byline: Businessman and Araliya Group Chairman Dudley Sirisena has pledged to provide Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga with world-class javelins almost every year until he achieves his goal of winning an Olympic gold medal for Sri Lanka.

title: TikTok founder becomes Asia’s richest person, overtakes Adani: Top 20
byline: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming has become Asia’s richest person for the first time, overtaking Indian billionaire Gautam Adani as his fortune crossed $105 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

title: Rabies bill could derail dog vaccination drive, raise human rabies risk: PHIs
byline: The proposed Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill could potentially disrupt Sri Lanka’s dog vaccination programme and increase the risk of human rabies, the Sri Lanka Public Health Inspectors Association (SLPHIA) has warned.

title: EU announces plan to ban social media for under 13s
byline: The European Union is moving to ban social media for under 13s across the bloc and impose restrictions on the digital technology for older children, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced Wednesday.

title: NPP to slow down President’s islandwide rallies
byline: The Government has decided to space out the series of islandwide public rallies scheduled to be attended by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Agriculture Minister K.D. Lal Kantha said today.

title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
byline: The Kosovo war crimes tribunal has convicted former Kosovar President Hashim Thaci of four counts of war crimes committed during his country’s war for independence from Serbia.

title: CSE selling deepens as ASPI breaks below 21,200
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its decline for a third consecutive session on 16 September 2026, with broad-based selling intensifying as elevated global oil prices continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

title: Supermarkets in Bandaragama, Matugama fined for overpriced eggs, altered prices
byline: Two supermarket branches in Bandaragama and Matugama have been fined a total of Rs. 400,000 in two separate cases for selling eggs above the marked price, altering original prices on food products and offering expired beverages for sale.

title: Railway Operating Service Union supports Sept. 17-18 action
byline: The Railway Technological and Operating Service Union has announced that it will join the joint trade union action scheduled for September 17 and 18, while calling for the intervention of the authorities over issues affecting the railway service.

title: A helmet, a lesson and a safer ride to school
byline: For some children in Nuwara Eliya, the start of the new school term came with an unexpected but important gift a helmet to help keep them safe on their daily journey to school.

title: Gold mine collapse kills at least 70 people in Sudan’s West Kordofan
byline: At least 70 people have been killed after a gold mine collapsed in Sudan’s West Kordofan state.

title: Two killed, several injured in Mattakkuliya accident
byline: Two people were killed and several others injured in a collision involving a car, a three-wheeler and four motorcycles in Mattakkuliya tonight (16).

title: Veterinary surgeon attacked by leopard
byline: The wildlife veterinary surgeon who attempted to save a hill country leopard caught in a wire trap had a harrowing experience this morning when it sprang at him causing him Injuries.

title: Shortage of crepe bandages reported at Colombo National Hospital
byline: A shortage of essential surgical supplies, including crepe bandages, at the Colombo National Hospital and other major hospitals has sparked concern over the country’s medical supply system, with patients reportedly being asked to purchase items needed for their treatment from outside pharmacies.
